title: Go Programming
description: Beginner-to-advanced Go reference covering values, slices, maps, structs, interfaces, generics, errors, context, goroutines, channels, synchronization, modules, testing, profiling, security, and production services.

subtopics.title: Values, Control Flow & Functions
subtopics.description: Go favors explicit control flow, zero values, short declarations inside functions, and multiple return values for results plus errors.

callouts.title: Shadowing Is Easy
callouts.text: := may create a new inner variable instead of assigning the intended outer variable. Keep scopes small and inspect declarations in error-handling blocks.

subtopics.title: Arrays, Slices & Maps
subtopics.description: Arrays have fixed length in their type; slices are views over backing arrays; maps are reference-like hash tables whose iteration order is unspecified.

rows: Concurrent writes and missing-key zero values

codeBlocks.code:
items := make([]string, 0, 8)
items = append(items, "a", "b")
copyOfItems := append([]string(nil), items...)

counts := map[string]int{}
counts["ready"]++
value, ok := counts["missing"]

callouts.title: Copy at Ownership Boundaries
callouts.text: A subslice can retain a large backing array and callers can mutate shared elements. Copy when storing untrusted caller-owned slices or returning internal mutable data.

subtopics.title: Structs, Methods & Pointers
subtopics.description: Structs compose data; methods attach behavior to named types. Use pointer receivers for mutation or large values and keep receiver choice consistent.

callouts.title: Embedding Is Promotion, Not Inheritance
callouts.text: Embedded fields promote methods and fields but do not create subtype inheritance. Prefer explicit composition when promoted APIs would blur ownership.

subtopics.title: Interfaces & Composition
subtopics.description: Types satisfy interfaces implicitly. Define small interfaces near consumers and accept behavior while returning useful concrete types.

callouts.title: Typed nil Inside an Interface Is Not nil
callouts.text: An interface is nil only when both dynamic type and value are absent. Avoid returning typed nil pointers as interface values.

subtopics.title: Generics & Constraints
subtopics.description: Use type parameters when one implementation preserves relationships across multiple concrete types. Constraints describe permitted operations, not runtime interfaces.

callouts.title: Prefer Ordinary Functions Until Repetition Is Real
callouts.text: Generics are strongest for containers and algorithms. An interface may better express behavior, while duplication may be clearer for two unrelated domain operations.

subtopics.title: Errors, Wrapping, defer & panic
subtopics.description: Return errors for expected failures, wrap them with context, inspect with errors.Is/As, and reserve panic for unrecoverable invariant violations.

callouts.title: defer Arguments Evaluate Immediately
callouts.text: Deferred function arguments are captured when defer executes. Deferred calls run in last-in-first-out order when the surrounding function returns.

subtopics.title: Goroutines & Lifetime Ownership
subtopics.description: Every goroutine needs an owner, termination condition, bounded resource use, and a way to communicate failure or cancellation.

callouts.title: A Goroutine Is Not Automatically Structured
callouts.text: A go statement detaches lifetime unless the caller waits and cancels it. Avoid fire-and-forget work in request handlers and libraries.

subtopics.title: Channels, select & Backpressure
subtopics.description: Channels communicate ownership or events. The sender normally closes; receivers range until closure; select coordinates readiness, cancellation, and timeouts.

callouts.title: Do Not Close from the Receiver
callouts.text: Closing asserts that no more values will be sent. Multiple senders require one coordinating owner; sending to or closing an already closed channel panics.

subtopics.title: Mutexes, Atomics & Context
subtopics.description: Protect shared invariants with mutexes, use atomics for narrow measured cases, and pass context as the first parameter for cancellation and deadlines.

callouts.title: Do Not Store Context in Structs
callouts.text: Pass context per operation, do not use it for optional parameters, and always call returned cancel functions to release timers and child references.

subtopics.title: Modules, Packages & Toolchain
subtopics.description: Modules version dependency graphs; packages define compilation/API boundaries. Commit go.mod and go.sum and make the supported Go language/toolchain policy explicit.

codeBlocks.code:
go mod init example.com/service
go get example.com/dependency@v1.2.3
go mod tidy
go list -m -u all
go vet ./...
go fix ./...

callouts.title: Go 1.26 Modernizes go fix
callouts.text: Review go fix changes like any automated migration. Run formatting, vet, tests, race checks, and benchmarks before accepting generated modernizations.

subtopics.title: Tests, Fuzzing, Race Detection & Benchmarks
subtopics.description: Use table-driven tests for cases, fuzzing for invariants, the race detector for executed concurrency paths, and benchmarks with allocation reporting.

codeBlocks.code:
go test ./...
go test -race ./...
go test -fuzz=FuzzParse ./parser
go test -bench=. -benchmem ./...
go test -coverprofile=coverage.out ./...

callouts.title: Race-Free Does Not Mean Correct
callouts.text: The race detector observes only executed paths and cannot prove higher-level ordering or atomicity invariants. Design synchronization first, then test it under load.

subtopics.title: HTTP Services, Profiling & Checklist
subtopics.description: Configure server timeouts and graceful shutdown, propagate request context, bound bodies and concurrency, expose health separately, and profile before optimizing.

callouts.title: Production Checklist
callouts.text: Pin supported Go versions, format/vet/test/race in CI, bound goroutines and I/O, propagate context, wrap errors, avoid data races, set HTTP/database timeouts, redact secrets, profile release binaries, and rehearse graceful shutdown.
